editions.label: Thursday, 12 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates are marked.

stories.title: David Jones names 19 stores to close, including Macquarie Centre
stories.summary: David Jones’s receiver has confirmed that 19 of its 38 stores will shut. Seven are in NSW, including Macquarie Centre, Parramatta and Hornsby, all relevant if you shop around Epping. This is the first confirmed list since the retailer entered administration.
stories.detail: The affected stores are expected to trade through the peak shopping period. Exact closure dates were not given; the company says stock will either be discounted or moved to other stores.

stories.title: NSW premier and ministers subpoenaed over Town Hall protest
stories.summary: Chris Minns, Police Minister Yasmin Catley, Tourism Minister Steve Kamper and senior police have been subpoenaed in the case against people charged over February’s Sydney Town Hall protest. Defence lawyers want to ask how the policing operation was planned and what role ministers played.
stories.detail: ABC reports the subpoenas seek evidence on 8 March, five days before the NSW election. The defence’s claims of improper interference are allegations, not findings; the ministers’ offices declined to comment because the case is before the court.

stories.title: Centennial Park uses beneficial insects to protect its roses
stories.summary: Centennial Park’s horticulture team is using ladybirds and small parasitic wasps to manage aphids in its historic rose garden. It’s an annual intervention, not a one-off experiment, and ABC reports the current infestation has been particularly heavy.
stories.detail: The garden overlooks Busbys Pond and has about 800 plants across 33 rose varieties. If you’re looking for a small stop on a ride or walk through the park, that’s where to find it.

stories.title: Apple Invites adds polls for guests
stories.summary: The latest Apple Invites update lets hosts add a poll so guests can vote on details such as food or a party theme. There’s also a decorative emoji effect, but the poll is the useful change if you want to settle a choice without a group chat.
stories.detail: Hosts still need iCloud+ to create an event. Guests can RSVP from the invitation link without paying or owning an Apple device; Apple Invites is listed in the Australian App Store.

stories.title: Finland clears Tesla’s supervised driver assistance
stories.summary: Finland’s transport regulator recognised the provisional approval granted by the Netherlands for Tesla Assisted Driving, the European name for FSD (Supervised). Tesla says the Finnish rollout will begin soon, which is distinct from the regulatory permission already in place.
stories.detail: The driver remains responsible. This is a Finnish decision, not EU-wide approval, and it does not establish any new feature or eligibility for your Australian Model Y.
stories.source: Not a Tesla App, citing Traficom and Tesla

stories.title: Musk extends the Cybertruck production timetable
stories.summary: Elon Musk says Tesla will now build Cybertrucks through the end of the US summer in 2027, later than the previously reported June or July shutdown. Not a Tesla App reports the extension gives the Texas line more time to work through existing orders.
stories.detail: It is not a reversal of the decision to end production or a promise that all deposits will turn into deliveries. No change to the cancellation of Australian reservations was announced.
stories.source: Not a Tesla App, citing Elon Musk

stories.title: Gemini Live starts rolling out on Apple CarPlay
stories.summary: Google is rolling out the standalone Gemini Live experience on compatible CarPlay displays globally in supported languages. It can pick up recent conversations from your iPhone and, with connected Workspace apps, help you talk through a calendar or inbox. The rollout announcement does not guarantee it has reached every Australian account yet.
stories.detail: This is a CarPlay feature, not a Tesla infotainment update. If you have access in a compatible car, one idea is to rehearse an executive review while parked using a sanitised brief, then pick up the conversation on your phone.
stories.published: 11 Nov, source date; reported 12 Nov, 4:29 am Sydney time

stories.title: SwitchBot puts a removable battery on its retrofit curtain motor
stories.summary: The new Curtain Track 4 fits existing U-rail curtains and lets you remove the Battery+ module for USB-C charging without taking the motor off the rail. It doesn’t fit curtain rods. A compatible SwitchBot hub is needed to bring it into Apple Home through Matter.
stories.detail: It’s available through the US channels cited by 9to5Mac; Australian pricing and stock were not confirmed. Check the rail and hub requirements before ordering.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia agree to a large prisoner exchange
stories.summary: Negotiators from both sides confirmed a planned prisoner-of-war swap after two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. That is a concrete outcome from the talks covered yesterday, but not a ceasefire or a settlement of the territorial dispute.
stories.detail: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are due to meet Vladimir Putin in Moscow, then Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin. A timetable for the exchange was not given in the ABC report.

stories.title: Albanese calls for more Pacific climate support at COP31
stories.summary: At the leaders’ summit in Antalya, Anthony Albanese urged countries to help Pacific nations adapt to climate change, pointing to the Pacific Resilience Facility. The appeal came as climate advocates challenged Australia’s support for new coal and gas projects.
stories.detail: The intervention puts Pacific climate finance alongside the argument over how to cut fossil fuel use. Negotiations are still under way; the speech was a call for action, not a new funding agreement.

stories.title: Spain’s housing crisis triggers its first general strike since 2012
stories.summary: Spanish unions say four million people joined a national strike over housing affordability, as tenants’ groups protested rising rents and evictions. The walkout came less than three weeks before the snap general election on 29 November.
stories.detail: Housing was already shaping the election after parliament rejected measures aimed at limiting rent pressure and curbing evictions. The turnout figure is the unions’ estimate.

editions.label: Wednesday, 11 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates are marked.

stories.title: Newcastle IVF patients face uncertainty over hospital takeover
stories.summary: Calvary Health Care says it will not allow IVF egg collections at hospitals it acquires from Healthscope, a proposed deal that includes Newcastle Private and Hunter Valley Private. Hunter IVF uses Newcastle Private’s operating theatres, but Calvary does not own the fertility clinic or its embryo lab.
stories.detail: Hunter IVF says it is working with alternative providers to avoid interruptions, but where some time-sensitive procedures would take place is still unclear. The takeover needs a NSW hospital licence and a decision from the competition regulator.

stories.title: NSW approves 1.4 GW wind farm near Hay
stories.summary: The Independent Planning Commission has approved the Baldon Wind Farm in the state’s South West Renewable Energy Zone. The project allows 175 turbines up to 300 metres tall, with conditions on road upgrades, traffic and rehabilitation after substantial community opposition.
stories.detail: Planning approval does not mean 1.4 GW is about to reach the grid. Baldon missed out on the zone’s initial transmission access allocation, so its full generating capacity and its ability to deliver that power are separate questions.

stories.title: Apple TV adds on-screen sign language for selected films
stories.summary: Apple announced that viewers will be able to turn on a synchronised interpreter for Being Heumann and F1: The Movie from Friday, with more titles to follow. The initial options are American and British Sign Language, not Auslan.
stories.detail: The controls appear on supported titles after enabling Sign Language in the TV app settings. The report confirms iPhone, iPad and Mac on version 27.2 or later, plus some other app platforms, but does not establish support for the first-generation Apple TV 4K or a separate Australian rollout.

stories.title: Tesla closes orders for another Cybertruck trim
stories.summary: Tesla has stopped taking US orders for the Premium AWD Cybertruck, leaving the Cyberbeast as the only orderable trim, according to Not a Tesla App. It also increased the Cyberbeast’s listed price by US$7,500 to US$109,990.
stories.detail: This is a new change to the US ordering page during the production wind-down, rather than another announcement of the wind-down itself. Tesla has not said whether Premium AWD orders will reopen, and the change does not affect the Australian Model Y line-up.

stories.title: Claude adds collaborative whiteboards and spreadsheets
stories.summary: Anthropic has launched Whiteboards and Sheets in beta on paid plans, while Claude Dashboards becomes generally available as Claude Data. The new tools let teams organise notes into a shared board, edit a spreadsheet together and build reports from connected data. Some Claude Data features, including certified queries and live sharing, are still in beta.
stories.detail: For a customer workshop, try a sanitised whiteboard that groups ideas and turns decisions into actions with owners and dates, then review it before sharing. Team plans have the tools on by default, while Enterprise availability depends on admin settings. Anthropic did not specify a separate Australian launch date.

stories.title: Google opens Gemini 4 Carbon to more users
stories.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available through Google’s API for paying developers and enterprises, with a rollout to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode and Antigravity. Google positions Carbon for demanding, longer tasks, including analysing documents with charts and tables.
stories.detail: It is a broader paid release, not confirmation of access on lower tiers or immediate availability on every Australian account. Google still positions Argon as the everyday option for most knowledge work.

stories.title: Garmin can alert nearby Waze drivers to a cyclist
stories.summary: Garmin has added an opt-in Waze integration for outdoor rides recorded on compatible Edge computers and watches. When a rider shares their LiveTrack position through Garmin Connect, nearby Waze drivers can see a moving alert. Garmin says personal information is not displayed and sharing is limited to the ride session.
stories.detail: It could be useful on road rides if you have compatible gear and are comfortable sharing your live position. It does not alert drivers using other navigation apps, and the release did not specify a separate Australian rollout date.

stories.title: TSMC approves up to US$1 billion in AI investments
stories.summary: TSMC’s board approved up to US$500 million in Anthropic shares at its IPO price and up to US$500 million in OpenAI preferred stock, Reuters reports. The move would give the chipmaker an ownership stake in two major AI developers as well as exposure through its manufacturing business.
stories.detail: The board approvals are investment limits, not confirmation that the full amounts have changed hands.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia resume US-brokered talks without a breakthrough
stories.summary: Envoys from Ukraine, Russia and the US met in Abu Dhabi for their first such talks since February. They discussed security guarantees and territorial concessions, but the sides remain far apart and no ceasefire was announced.
stories.detail: Kyiv is seeking security guarantees, while Moscow wants to address a broader European security framework first. European representatives met separately with Ukrainian and US officials, underscoring the disagreement over who should be involved in a settlement.

stories.title: COP31 electrification pledge runs into a fossil fuel dispute
stories.summary: Türkiye’s proposal to lift electricity to 35 per cent of global energy use by 2035 is meeting resistance because its draft wording does not require the extra electricity to be clean. Critics say the pledge could prolong fossil fuel use if countries meet it with more coal or gas power.
stories.detail: Australia is separately pushing to double the number of households with rooftop solar to at least 300 million by 2030. Both are proposals, not final summit commitments.

afternoon.note: Afternoon developments checked in Sydney local time. Quiet categories are omitted.

stories.title: NSW to recruit 129 hospital security staff
stories.summary: The NSW government says it will recruit 129 additional security staff across 27 hospitals. The announcement follows an alleged attack on a nurse and a doctor at Concord Hospital, where one staff member suffered a broken wrist.
stories.detail: Police say the patient remains in hospital and the incident is under investigation. Health Minister Ryan Park is considering additional powers for security staff, but has not made a decision.

stories.title: Apple Support Community set to close on 20 November
stories.summary: A notice on Apple's support forums says the community will permanently close on 20 November, and new posts are already disabled. Existing discussions can currently be read and searched, but new questions and replies cannot be submitted.
stories.detail: That removes a long-running source of peer troubleshooting for Apple devices. It is unclear whether the existing archive will remain accessible after closure; 9to5Mac has asked Apple to clarify the scope.

stories.title: Russia reports a fresh drone attack on Leningrad region
stories.summary: The regional governor says Russia shot down 92 drones over the Leningrad region early on Wednesday. Reuters could not independently verify the claim. The region contains major Baltic export ports and the Kirishi oil refinery.
stories.detail: Latvia and Lithuania warned residents to seek shelter from unidentified drones entering their airspace, and NATO air defence fighters were activated. The reports come as Russia and Ukraine hold US-brokered talks, but do not establish any change in the negotiations.

editions.label: Tuesday, 10 November 2026
editions.note: Times are Sydney local unless noted. Material updates are marked; categories without noteworthy developments are omitted.

stories.title: ASIC opens a formal investigation into Bathla
stories.summary: Australia’s corporate regulator has moved from preliminary scrutiny to a formal investigation into the affairs of the collapsed Sydney developer. ASIC has not specified the conduct it is investigating and says its separate inquiries into private lenders have not yet become a formal investigation.
stories.detail: The new step matters for buyers and contractors because the group’s collapse has put more than 200 projects in doubt, including about 2,000 homes under construction. The investigation does not set a timetable for construction to restart or for creditors to recover money.

stories.title: NSW report finds a gap in who gets diverted from court
stories.summary: The NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research found Aboriginal children were 30 per cent less likely than non-Aboriginal children to receive a police diversion from court. The gap persisted for alleged offences eligible for diversion, which can take the form of a warning, caution or intervention.
stories.detail: Even after accounting for factors such as offence severity, prior contact and bail status, Aboriginal children were about eight percentage points more likely to be taken to court. The researchers could not explain that remaining gap from their data; the Aboriginal Legal Service says it points to bias.

stories.title: Apple patches Messages, AirPlay and Bluetooth flaws
stories.summary: Apple has released iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 alongside macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1 and patches for some older versions. The iPhone fixes include an issue that could let a remote attacker join an iMessage group chat uninvited and another that could let an attacker within Bluetooth range bypass AirPlay pairing-code limits.
stories.detail: This is a security and bug-fix release, not the upcoming feature update. Check Software Update on your iPhone and Mac for the patch on the software branch you’re actually using.

stories.title: Apple starts selling extra AI usage in Logic Pro
stories.summary: The latest Logic Pro update adds a one-off US$49.99 purchase for extra usage of eligible intelligence features, according to 9to5Mac. The extra allowance is used only after the monthly limit, expires after 12 months and cannot be shared through Family Sharing.
stories.detail: Logic Pro is the first confirmed app with the purchase option. Other Creator Studio apps are expected to follow, but this is not a charge for system-wide Apple Intelligence. Australian pricing and availability were not independently confirmed.

stories.title: Tesla opens Model Y Robotaxi rides in San Antonio
stories.summary: Tesla opened Robotaxi rides in San Antonio at 5 am Texas time on 9 November, or 10 pm in Sydney. Not a Tesla App reports that the service uses Model Ys and has Tesla’s largest advertised launch area, around 710 square kilometres.
stories.detail: The mapped area is not a guarantee that every pickup or drop-off is bookable. This is a US fleet rollout, not a feature release for privately owned Model Ys or a confirmation of an Australian Robotaxi launch.
stories.source: Not a Tesla App, citing Tesla Robotaxi
stories.published: 9 Nov US date; rides began 10 pm Sydney time

stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
stories.summary: Anthropic says the upgraded models improve coding, reasoning and visual tasks and generate outputs up to 30 per cent faster than their predecessors. Fable 5.2 is available on Claude and the major cloud platforms, subject to plan access. Mythos access remains restricted for specialist use, and Australian cloud-region availability was not separately confirmed.
stories.detail: For a practical trial in an approved workspace, give Fable a sanitised QBR pack and ask it to flag where proposed slide claims disagree with the source numbers, with a citation for each flag. Anthropic still recommends Opus 5.5 for most everyday work, so reserve Fable for the tricky review rather than every follow-up.
stories.published: 9 Nov US date; reported 10 Nov, 6:03 am Sydney time

stories.title: Google adds two chips for private and long-context AI
stories.summary: Google announced TPU 8tx for workloads that need data and model weights protected while being processed, and TPU 8i Max for tasks that need to keep much more information in memory. The latter combines two TPU 8i chips in one package, doubling compute and memory bandwidth versus a single TPU 8i, according to Google.
stories.detail: Think regulated workloads for the first and large codebases or hours of video for the second. The announcement did not specify an Australian rollout date.

stories.title: Republican congressman files articles to impeach Hegseth
stories.summary: US Republican Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday in Washington. That turns the pressure covered yesterday into a formal, immediate House bid rather than a possible effort after the next Congress takes office.
stories.detail: ABC reports the move starts a two-day clock for the House to act. Filing articles is not the same as the House voting to impeach or the Senate voting to remove him.

stories.title: Victoria’s Big Build inquiry begins public hearings
stories.summary: The royal commission’s opening day examined a 2022 work stoppage at a Sunbury level crossing project. It heard evidence that contractor John Holland was wary of the CFMEU’s perceived access to Victorian ministers, alongside allegations of threats against subcontractors.
stories.detail: The commission is testing those claims, not making findings at this stage. The public hearings are due to run until 20 November, just over a week before Victoria’s state election.

stories.title: Russell Brand sentenced to 10 years and six months
stories.summary: A London court has sentenced Russell Brand to 10 years and six months in prison after his conviction for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The offences involved four women and occurred between 2004 and 2009.
stories.detail: The sentence is the new development following last week’s jury verdict.

afternoon.note: Afternoon developments checked in Sydney local time. Quiet categories are omitted.

stories.title: Mental health patients wait up to six days in Westmead's emergency department
stories.summary: ABC reports that 12 people with acute mental illness had waited more than 48 hours in Westmead Hospital's emergency department as of Monday afternoon, with the longest wait exceeding six days. A doctor described the situation as potentially dangerous.
stories.detail: The local health district says patients awaiting transfer continue to receive treatment under a psychiatrist and apologised for extended waits. The NSW mental health minister says a new Westmead facility under construction will increase regional bed capacity.

stories.title: NSW introduces bill to allow higher coal output after court ruling
stories.summary: The Minns government has introduced legislation to let the Mount Pleasant mine in the Hunter Valley produce up to 16.5 million tonnes a year until 2032. It follows a High Court decision that invalidated its expansion approval because overseas emissions had not been considered.
stories.detail: The mine's original permit allows 12.5 million tonnes annually. The government says the bill addresses legal uncertainty and protects jobs; opponents say it bypasses the court process. Debate has been adjourned and the bill is not yet law.

stories.title: Australia plans an AI safety regulator and mandatory incident reporting
stories.summary: The federal government has accepted all 18 recommendations of its review into an OpenAI agent's access to a Medicare statistics portal. It plans mandatory safety and security standards, incident reporting and a regulator able to impose penalties and require independent model evaluations.
stories.detail: The proposed legislation is planned for introduction next year, so the rules are not yet in force. The government says no personal information was accessed; the review also recommends considering changes to criminal law. For organisations adopting AI agents, the direction points towards stronger incident reporting and oversight expectations.

stories.title: Qantas to cut 850 corporate roles in Accenture deal
stories.summary: Qantas says it will cut 850 corporate positions over coming years as it outsources work under a multi-year partnership with Accenture. Finance, procurement and marketing are first affected, with services to be delivered mostly by teams in India and some in Australia.
stories.detail: The first changes are expected by mid-2027, and Qantas says it will seek to redeploy as many employees as possible. The airline says the deal will also help modernise its technology and accelerate its use of AI.

editions.label: Monday, 9 November 2026
editions.note: Checked Monday morning, Sydney time. Publication times below are Sydney time. Reported plans, rumours and unverified claims are labelled; the AI release section is short on a quiet weekend.

stories.title: Victoria Barracks stays public after a government backdown
stories.summary: Anthony Albanese has scrapped the planned sale of Sydney's Victoria Barracks following a political and community backlash. The heritage site will instead transfer from Defence to the Finance Department, with the prime minister promising public access and protection of its history.
stories.detail: This reverses part of Saturday's defence-property sale story. Three other sites are also being retained, but Defence personnel are still due to leave all 67 affected properties within two years. The wider disposal programme continues; unrestricted public access is not yet confirmed.

stories.title: Bathla workers seek answers over missing wages and entitlements
stories.summary: About 200 former Bathla workers are demanding clarity over unpaid wages and entitlements after the Sydney developer's collapse. Employees speaking publicly for the first time describe debts running into tens of thousands of dollars, difficulty finding new jobs and, for some, uncertainty about their immigration status.
stories.detail: Bathla entered voluntary administration in August owing at least $3.4 billion. Administrators have been granted until September 2027 to determine the group's future, leaving staff facing a lengthy wait. Today's development is the workers' accounts and demands for transparent entitlement information, rather than a newly announced collapse or a confirmed repayment timetable.

stories.title: Cooks River data centre dropped, but logistics plans continue
stories.summary: Stockland and John Boyd Properties have removed the AI data centre from their proposed redevelopment of the former Kogarah Golf Club site at Arncliffe. Community opponents had raised concerns about the Cooks River's ecology, electricity demand, water use and noise.
stories.detail: The partners say they are still pursuing the logistics precinct, so this is not the cancellation of the whole development. Their revised plans include a public foreshore connection and future parkland. It is a concrete local example of the infrastructure pressures behind the broader NSW data-centre debate, distinct from last week's parliamentary inquiry findings.

stories.title: Sydney's abrupt chill brings November snow to the mountains
stories.summary: A strong cold front has brought snow to parts of NSW and a sharp temperature drop across Sydney. ABC reports the city fell from 29.7C on Saturday to 14C that evening, while Thredbo reached minus 5C overnight.
stories.detail: Strong southerly winds and hazardous coastal conditions are forecast for Monday, with the chill continuing. If you're heading out from Epping, take a warmer layer.

stories.title: Report: Siri could become more proactive next year
stories.summary: 9to5Mac reports that Bloomberg's Mark Gurman expects Apple to move towards a more agent-like Siri, potentially as early as next year. The idea is an assistant that can pursue goals and decide what to do next, rather than needing a separate instruction for every step.
stories.detail: This is fresh reporting about Apple's direction, not an announced release or an available feature. There is no confirmed launch date, supported-device list or Australian rollout to act on. For you, the interesting prospect is less manual coordination across apps, but it would be premature to build a customer workflow around it.

stories.title: Musk outlines a smaller-battery, silver Cybercab
stories.summary: Not a Tesla App reports that Elon Musk says upcoming efficiency improvements will allow a 40kWh Cybercab battery, down from the current 47.6kWh pack. He also says Tesla will offer the robotaxi in liquid silver alongside gold.
stories.detail: No timing or revised range figures were supplied. A smaller pack could reduce manufacturing cost and weight, but that is a potential implication, not a measured outcome for the new version. This concerns Cybercab hardware: no corresponding Australian Model Y battery change, software update or local robotaxi launch is confirmed. The published silver images are concepts, not proof of delivered vehicles.
stories.source: Not a Tesla App, reporting Musk's announcement

stories.title: No significant fresh AI release verified
stories.summary: No significant new AI model or practical product release with verified availability was found in the past 24 hours. Older announcements are not being recycled as new releases.
stories.detail: My suggestion for an existing approved tool: extract commitments, owners and dates from a sanitised transcript, then verify them before drafting a follow-up. This is a workflow idea, not a new feature.

stories.title: Report: Anthropic secures US$3.4 billion in power equipment
stories.summary: Reuters, citing the Financial Times, reports that Anthropic secured commitments for 1.7GW of gas-fired generators from OnePWR Solutions in late September. The reported deal includes installation-related engineering and construction capabilities, not an acquisition of the supplier.
stories.detail: Reuters could not independently verify the report, and neither company responded to its requests for comment. This is newly reported infrastructure spending, not a new Claude product or evidence that all the capacity is already operating. It underlines how power supply is shaping the AI industry's expansion.

stories.title: Hormuz shipping incidents continue as diplomacy inches forward
stories.summary: ABC reports that Iran says tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, while the US says it disabled a vessel attempting to breach its blockade. Iranian officials have not confirmed that explosions around Qeshm Island were new US strikes.
stories.detail: Iran is reviewing proposals conveyed through Qatar, but conditions for nuclear negotiations remain contested. Treat military claims and the cause of the blasts cautiously. For Australia, disruption to this major energy-shipping route remains relevant to fuel costs and supply chains; these reports do not establish a new local petrol-price change.

stories.title: Hegseth faces congressional pressure after the US midterms
stories.summary: ABC reports that multiple Democrats plan to pursue impeachment of US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth when they take control of both houses in January. It comes as Donald Trump reshapes his team, replacing chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller.
stories.detail: Hegseth's support for the unpopular Iran war is a major political vulnerability, according to the report. Speculation that Trump might dismiss him is not a confirmed decision, and threatened impeachment is not removal from office. The substantive development is the looming confrontation over defence leadership and war policy, rather than another recap of the election result.

stories.title: Seven killed in a train collision near Cairo
stories.summary: Egypt's health ministry says at least seven people were killed and more than 110 injured when passenger trains collided in Giza province on Sunday. One train struck the rear of another in Al-Ayyat, causing a derailment.
stories.detail: Emergency teams were sent to clear the wreckage and restore services. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi ordered an investigation. The technical cause has not yet been established.
stories.source: ABC News with AP and Reuters

afternoon.note: Developments since the 8:24am morning check. Publication times are Sydney time.

stories.title: Lamarre-Condon denies intending to kill Jesse Baird
stories.summary: Under cross-examination on Monday, former NSW police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon denied the prosecution's allegation that he intended to kill his former partner Jesse Baird. He also said the gun discharged during a struggle when Luke Davies was shot.
stories.detail: The testimony puts intent at the centre of the competing accounts in the double murder trial. Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty.

stories.title: Two NSW police officers charged after alleged e-bike hit and run
stories.summary: Detectives charged two constables on Monday over a May collision near Glebe Point Road. NSW Police allege a marked police vehicle hit a 25-year-old e-bike rider and the officers drove away without stopping to help.
stories.detail: The officer alleged to have been driving also faces a negligent driving charge. Both officers are due in court on 15 January, and NSW Police is reviewing their employment status.

stories.title: Apple Intelligence clears a registration step for iPads and Macs in China
stories.summary: Shanghai's cyberspace regulator says it has registered Apple Intelligence for use on tablets and laptops in China. This extends the regulatory progress beyond iPhones, which received approval in July.
stories.detail: Registration is required before public availability in China. The regulator's announcement gives no rollout date and concerns the Chinese market.

stories.title: Musk says Tesla will have to refund many Cybertruck deposits
stories.summary: Elon Musk said on Monday that Tesla expects to return deposits to many Cybertruck buyers because it cannot build enough pickups before the Texas line shuts. The refund expectation is new after the weekend's plan to add a production shift to clear the backlog.
stories.detail: Tesla has yet to give affected buyers a timetable in the reporting. The change concerns Cybertruck orders, with no announced effect on Australian Model Y owners.

stories.title: Senate questions TikTok over self-harm content
stories.summary: Independent senator David Pocock questioned TikTok executives on Monday about self-harm content during a hearing on Australia's proposed digital duty of care. The bill would put a greater onus on online platforms to protect users from harm.
stories.detail: The hearing put TikTok's handling of harmful content under scrutiny as senators consider what the proposed duty would require of platforms.

stories.title: Mitsui Chemicals strikes US$11.6 billion deal for chip materials maker JSR
stories.summary: Mitsui Chemicals agreed to buy JSR in a deal worth about US$11.6 billion, with backing from the Development Bank of Japan. The filing confirms a sale that Reuters had reported was in the works last week.
stories.detail: JSR makes photoresists, the light-sensitive materials used to transfer circuit patterns onto semiconductor wafers. The deal brings a key chipmaking supplier into a larger Japanese chemicals group.

stories.title: COP31 opens in Türkiye with a push to electrify more of the economy
stories.summary: The UN climate summit opened in Antalya on Monday, with Türkiye asking countries to back a pledge to electrify more than a third of the global economy by 2035. Australia is leading the negotiations.
stories.detail: The pledge has already drawn criticism because it leaves countries free to generate the extra electricity from fossil fuels. That makes the source of the power a point of debate alongside the headline target.

stories.title: Iran defends two-day path to talks after US rejects conditions
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry publicly defended a proposal on Monday to restart talks within two days, shortening its earlier seven-day proposal. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected some of Tehran's conditions, which include lifting sanctions and the naval blockade and ending hostilities.
stories.detail: The shorter timetable still depends on Washington accepting those conditions, so the proposal offers no clear path to an imminent reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Drone attack sets Russian refinery ablaze before peace talks
stories.summary: The governor of Russia's Leningrad region said a Ukrainian drone attack set the Kirishi refinery ablaze on Monday and that falling debris killed a woman. Kirishi is Russia's second-largest refinery.
stories.detail: The attack came a day before Russian, Ukrainian and US negotiators are due to meet in Abu Dhabi for their first peace talks since February, with security guarantees high on the agenda.

stories.title: Poland to review gun permit rules after Krakow gunman dies
stories.summary: The gunman who killed six people in Krakow's market square has died in hospital. Poland's justice minister said investigators will continue looking into whether he acted alone or was influenced by a group.
stories.detail: The government will also review its gun permit requirements. Authorities said the gunman and his father both held permits.

editions.label: Sunday, 8 November 2026
editions.note: A quieter weekend for product releases, with fresh NSW reporting and significant overseas developments. All publication times below are Sydney time. Preliminary results and company plans are labelled.

stories.title: Psychiatrist calls for clinical control of prison mental health
stories.summary: Leading forensic psychiatrist Kerri Eagle says Justice Health, rather than prison officers, should lead the management of mentally ill NSW inmates. Her intervention follows an ABC investigation identifying dozens of coronial findings about failures in care since 2015.
stories.detail: Eagle is a Justice Health clinical director but spoke in a private capacity, so this is a reform proposal, not an announced government policy. Prison officers currently develop immediate support plans covering housing and observation for inmates in crisis. Corrective Services NSW says progress requires a coordinated, whole-of-government response. The central question is who holds clinical responsibility when an inmate needs urgent care.

stories.title: NSW weighs stronger controls on collision and slap sports
stories.summary: A parliamentary inquiry is examining whether collision-running, competitive slapping and bare-knuckle boxing should be formally classified as combat sports. Friday's hearing exposed a sharp split: the Combat Sports Authority wants stronger controls, while neurologist Rowena Mobbs urged a ban because of brain-injury risks.
stories.detail: Bare Knuckle Australia representatives said they were willing to collaborate on regulation, although organisers differed over how much intervention was appropriate. Collision-running and power-slap organisers did not appear. The inquiry's report is expected by Christmas, so no new rules have been adopted through this process yet. The immediate significance is the direction of NSW event regulation, not a change to ordinary community sport.

stories.title: Newcastle hosts a wet World Cup breakthrough for the Kiwis
stories.summary: New Zealand beat Tonga 34-10 in the Rugby League World Cup semi-final at Hunter Stadium in Newcastle. Kalyn Ponga returned from a broken arm to deliver a man-of-the-match performance in appalling weather.
stories.detail: The result sends the Kiwis into the final. ABC's match analysis credits their pressure and composure in the difficult conditions.

stories.title: No significant fresh Apple development verified
stories.summary: No significant Apple announcement or substantive new development was verified within the past 24 hours. Fresh accessory coverage, shopping offers and weekly recaps do not warrant padding out today's section.
stories.detail: The source link opens MacRumors' dated November archive.

stories.title: Tesla plans an extra Cybertruck shift before the line closes
stories.summary: The substantive update to yesterday's wind-down news: Elon Musk says Tesla will add a production shift to try to clear Cybertruck orders before dismantling the line around June or July 2027. The space is intended for expanded Cybercab production.
stories.detail: Musk says the backlog exceeds what Tesla can currently build before that deadline. This is a production plan, not confirmation that every order will be fulfilled. No change to Australian Model Y servicing, software or charging is confirmed by this announcement.

stories.title: A quiet day for verified AI releases
stories.summary: No significant new AI product release with verified availability was found in the past 24 hours. Recent releases already covered are not being recycled as new meeting, presentation or workflow tools.
stories.detail: The source link is OpenAI's official news index, checked alongside other major providers. No new Australian rollout is claimed today.

stories.title: Who Gives A Crap warns customers after marketing-provider breach
stories.summary: Who Gives A Crap notified customers on Saturday that an unnamed US marketing-software provider had suffered unauthorised access affecting Australian, UK and US customer data. Names, contact information, mailing addresses and total spend were involved, but the company says payment details, order details and passwords were not.
stories.detail: Access began on 30 October and was secured on 1 November; WGAC says it was informed on Friday. It does not yet know whether data was copied or downloaded and reports no evidence of misuse. It has disconnected the provider and changed credentials. My suggested CSM takeaway: use this as a prompt to review third-party access scope and incident-notification responsibilities with relevant teams. The reporting does not identify the vendor, so there is no basis to attribute it to Braze.

stories.title: New Zealand's election is too close to settle
stories.summary: With results from all voting places, National has 29.37 per cent of the party vote against Labour's 29.22 per cent. The National, ACT and NZ First bloc is provisionally projected to hold 67 of 131 seats, only one above the majority threshold.
stories.detail: About 700,000 special votes, including overseas ballots, remain to be processed. That means yesterday's voting has not produced a confirmed government, and both major-party leaders acknowledge negotiations lie ahead. Smaller parties and the final size of parliament could change the balance. Expect weeks of counting and coalition discussions, not a settled winner this weekend.

stories.title: Russian strikes damage Kyiv's energy supply and a major bridge
stories.summary: The attacks Ukraine warned about yesterday have now hit energy infrastructure around Kyiv, with authorities reporting serious pressure on electricity, water and heating as temperatures approach freezing. Missiles also damaged the Northern Bridge across the Dnipro.
stories.detail: Authorities reported at least two deaths and around a dozen injuries across Ukraine. The strikes come before US-brokered Russia-Ukraine talks scheduled in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November. This is a material escalation from the earlier warning, not a repeat of it.

stories.title: Eisenkot gets the first chance to form Israel's government
stories.summary: President Isaac Herzog has selected Benjamin Netanyahu's leading rival, Gadi Eisenkot, to try to assemble a coalition after Israel's deadlocked election. This does not make Eisenkot prime minister: he still needs a parliamentary majority.
stories.detail: The formal offer is expected later on Sunday in Israel, early Monday in Sydney, after which he will initially have 28 days. Arab-Israeli parties hold a record 19 seats and are central to the negotiations. Without their support, Eisenkot would need ultra-Orthodox parties from Netanyahu's previous coalition to change sides. The political outcome remains unresolved.

stories.title: Six killed in Krakow market-square shooting
stories.summary: Polish authorities say six people were killed and 16 injured in a shooting in Krakow's main market square. Police shot the suspected lone attacker, who remains in hospital, and say the public is now safe.
stories.detail: The interior minister says early findings point to far-right ideological influences, but the motive has not been established. One injured police officer is in a critical condition. Treat the ideological assessment and other early details as provisional while investigators establish what happened.

editions.label: Saturday, 7 November 2026
editions.note: Checked Saturday morning, Sydney time. Regional availability, preliminary findings and suggested applications are labelled.

stories.title: Bondi attack survivor Eva Geller dies
stories.summary: Eva Geller, 90, has died after being shot at the Bondi Chanukah gathering last December. ABC reports she was a Holocaust survivor who came to Australia from Hungary as a child and spent much of the past year in hospital or rehabilitation.
stories.detail: NSW Police say they are working with the coroner and awaiting further advice. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and NSW Premier Chris Minns paid tribute to Geller and offered condolences to her family and Sydney's Jewish community.

stories.title: Powerhouse Parramatta opens to the public today
stories.summary: Western Sydney's $915 million museum opens on Saturday with more than 3,000 objects and five major exhibitions. This is the public opening itself, following earlier previews of the works inside.
stories.detail: Entry and four of the five exhibitions are free. The ticketed space and aviation exhibition is $30 for adults, $20 for concessions and free for under-16s. Street parking is limited, so public transport is worth considering if you're heading over from Epping.

stories.title: AFP searches Tokyo flight after Sydney Airport threat
stories.summary: Armed federal police met passengers on an All Nippon Airways flight from Tokyo at Sydney Airport on Thursday night and carried out precautionary searches. A passenger told ABC people were kept on board for about 90 minutes before disembarking.
stories.detail: The AFP confirmed threats had been sent to an airport. Nearly 30 flights were disrupted by separate bomb threats across Europe on Thursday, but authorities have not established a link to Sydney, and no explosives were reported found on the aircraft searched.

stories.title: Apple Australia extends eligible online holiday returns
stories.summary: Eligible items received from Apple Australia's online store between 6 November and 25 December can be returned until 8 January 2027. The window is based on when you receive the item, not simply when you order it.
stories.detail: That gives you more time to decide on a gift or a new device bought directly from Apple. Other retailers have their own policies, and Apple excludes iPhones bought through carrier financing or carrier offers from the extension.

stories.title: Tesla plans to wind down Cybertruck production in Texas
stories.summary: Elon Musk says Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Austin-area factory around mid-2027 to make room for more Cybercabs. AP cites Kelley Blue Book estimates of about 20,200 Cybertruck sales in 2025 and a further 28 per cent fall through September this year.
stories.detail: It is a production plan, not an immediate stop or an Australian robotaxi rollout. The announcement does not confirm a change to Australian Model Y production, support or driver-assistance features.

stories.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small through Tinker
stories.summary: Thinking Machines Lab has made its new vision and reasoning model available in Tinker Playground and for fine-tuning and inference through Tinker. Downloadable weights are planned under Apache 2.0 after external safety testing, but they are not available yet; the announcement does not specify Australian account eligibility.
stories.detail: The lab demonstrated the model using visual feedback to refine interactive websites. My suggested test, if you have access: give it a screenshot of a mock customer review deck and ask it to flag slides where the takeaway is unclear, using dummy data rather than customer material.
stories.published: 5 Nov, vendor date; rollout reported 6 Nov AEDT

stories.title: EU says TikTok's For You feed may breach digital rules
stories.summary: The European Commission says TikTok has not adequately assessed or mitigated the risk of its feed repeatedly steering people towards similar material, including videos about body image or isolation. Regulators want changes to the recommender and easier controls for users to influence what they see.
stories.detail: These are preliminary findings under the Digital Services Act, not a final ruling. TikTok disputes the findings. Any resulting redesign could be worth watching in Australia, but no Australian product change was announced.

stories.title: Canberra presses ahead with defence property sales
stories.summary: The federal government is sticking with its plan to sell 67 Defence properties despite a parliamentary inquiry recommending a halt. ABC reports the sales are expected to bring in about $3 billion gross, or roughly $1.8 billion after remediation costs.
stories.detail: Sydney's Victoria Barracks is on the list, and both of Tasmania's live-fire training areas are earmarked for sale. The government argues that Defence should shift resources north and west, but it has yet to spell out how it will replace the Tasmanian training capacity.

stories.title: New Zealand votes in a tight general election
stories.summary: Polls are open today in New Zealand, where Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National Party and Christopher Hipkins's Labour Party are competing to lead the next government. Cost of living, housing affordability and sluggish growth have dominated the campaign.
stories.detail: Voting closes at 7 pm New Zealand time, or 5 pm in Sydney, with preliminary results released progressively afterwards. Those are not the final numbers: the official count, which includes special and overseas votes, is due on 27 November.

stories.title: Ukraine warns of fresh strikes on critical infrastructure
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukrainian intelligence indicates Russia is preparing new strikes on energy facilities, bridges and other infrastructure. He said the military was preparing for a difficult period.
stories.detail: The warning points to the risk of further disruption to essential services as winter approaches. It is an intelligence assessment reported by Ukraine's president, not confirmation that the anticipated strikes have already happened.

editions.label: Friday, 6 November 2026
editions.note: Checked Friday morning, Sydney time. Stories are deduplicated by underlying event. Releases, beta access, regional availability and suggested applications are labelled explicitly.

stories.title: NSW inquiry says data centre checks miss cumulative pressure
stories.summary: A cross-party NSW inquiry found planning assesses data centres largely as individual projects, missing their combined demands on electricity, water and infrastructure. Current guidance may underestimate future demand and the pressure created when facilities cluster.
stories.detail: The committee stopped short of a moratorium after members voted 6 to 1 to remove that recommendation. It instead called for a state strategy and better coordination across approvals. The issue is especially relevant around Sydney, where residents have opposed projects and major proposals remain under assessment.

stories.title: Sydney Mardi Gras party will return in 2027
stories.summary: The official post-parade party is coming back on 6 March beneath Sydney Football Stadium after this year's event was cancelled weeks before the parade. Organisers say the 2026 party would have cost about $2 million after running at a deficit since 2020.
stories.detail: The wider festival runs from 12 February to 7 March, one week longer than before. The performer line-up is due next Tuesday, member tickets open on 9 November and general and party pre-sales follow on 12 November.

stories.title: Apple Creator Studio's AI update is now rolling out
stories.summary: Apple has started releasing the Creator Studio update announced last month. It brings Generate Fill to Pixelmator Pro, a beta assistant and improved Stem Splitter to Logic Pro, plus context-aware beta assistants and MCP workflow support in Keynote, Pages and Numbers.
stories.detail: Final Cut Pro also gains built-in MotionVFX assets, a Content Hub and smoother Pixelmator Pro editing. The update is free for existing subscribers, but several AI features remain beta. Australian language or regional availability is not confirmed for every assistant, so check the app release notes before relying on them.

stories.title: First touchscreen MacBook Pro reviews are in
stories.summary: Early reviews praise the PROLED XDR tandem OLED display, slimmer design and lower weight, while treating touch as useful rather than transformative. Reviewers found gestures handy for photo work and media controls, but the laptop still behaves primarily like a conventional Mac.
stories.detail: Other changes include a Dynamic Island, redesigned cooling, up to 16TB of storage and revised speakers. The 14-inch and 16-inch models launch in Australia today from A$4,599 and A$5,499 respectively. For a recent MacBook Pro owner, the display and touch experience are the clearest reasons to upgrade.

stories.title: Model Y helps EVs outsell petrol for a third month
stories.summary: Battery electric vehicles took 23.1 per cent of Australia's new vehicle market in October and again outsold petrol-only cars. Tesla's Model Y and BYD's Sealion 7 were among the leading models, showing that electric SUVs are now driving a broad market shift rather than a niche surge.
stories.detail: This is Australian sales context, not a new Tesla feature, software release or change for an existing Model Y. It may strengthen the case for faster charging and service investment, but no owner-facing expansion was announced. No more significant worldwide Tesla product, autonomy, energy or regulatory development was verified in the past 24 hours.

stories.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber to a limited defender group
stories.summary: GPT-6 Cyber is a specialised model for finding, validating and helping patch exploitable software flaws while staying within authorised scope. OpenAI says it found 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities and helped develop working exploits for 948 Linux kernel issues, alongside candidate fixes.
stories.detail: The model is initially available only through the API and Codex to selected approved Daybreak Red customers, with broader Daybreak access planned. It is not a general ChatGPT release and no Australian availability is promised. For customer success work, the practical near-term implication is better automated security review by specialist teams, not a new everyday meeting or follow-up feature.

stories.title: Box announces a plain-language AI workflow builder
stories.summary: Box Architect will let teams describe a business process in ordinary language and turn it into an automated workflow. A related Nvidia-powered retrieval engine is intended to improve answers from company files while reducing token use and response time.
stories.detail: Architect is due to begin beta rollout this quarter for Enterprise Advanced customers, while Context Retrieval is slated for general availability in early 2027. No specific Australian launch was stated. Suggested experiment: describe a transcript-to-follow-up flow that extracts decisions, owners and risks, then drafts a customer email for review. That is my suggested use, not a reported Box deployment.

stories.title: AI accelerates both hacking and the race to patch
stories.summary: Nearly 37,000 software vulnerabilities were reported in the third quarter, triple the year-earlier level, as companies face faster and more sophisticated attacks. Reuters found firms are deploying AI monitoring and patching tools because exploitation can begin within hours of a flaw becoming public.
stories.detail: Recent cases include hacked European supermarket refrigeration systems and the record Binance theft. A security answer can date quickly, so ask vendors about patch speed, monitoring and incident response, not just certifications. This is an industry trend, separate from today's GPT-6 Cyber release.

stories.title: David Jones enters administration after months of payment strain
stories.summary: The 188-year-old department store entered voluntary administration on Thursday, while suppliers told ABC they had waited months for invoices and struggled to get calls answered. Its 38 stores will keep trading while administrators and receivers review the business.
stories.detail: McGrathNicol and FTI Consulting are examining options, with a creditors' meeting due next week. The immediate effect is uncertainty for suppliers, staff and gift-card holders rather than an announced shutdown. The collapse is a significant warning about pressure on discretionary retail before Christmas.

stories.title: Three more tankers are damaged in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran says three more tankers were damaged on Thursday, taking the number of vessel incidents reported since Sunday to at least five. The attacks keep a critical shipping route under pressure as the United States and Iran remain far apart on ending the Gulf conflict.
stories.detail: Qatari mediators say both sides are reviewing proposals, but no breakthrough has been announced on the strait, sanctions, the blockade or Iran's nuclear programme. Oil prices have fallen sharply as traders reassess the likelihood of renewed US strikes after the midterm result, though shipping risk remains high.

stories.title: Russell Brand is found guilty of rape and sexual assault
stories.summary: A London jury found the British comedian and actor guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two other rape charges and one attempted indecent assault charge after an eight-and-a-half-hour deliberation.
stories.detail: The judge revoked Brand's bail and said a significant custodial sentence was inevitable. He has been remanded in custody and will be sentenced on Monday. UK police say they are also investigating rape allegations made by two other women.
